messages:
maya: quick summary from today's quant bakeoff on open-7b-v2
chris: go on
maya: compared FP16, GPTQ, AWQ-8, and int8-linear across our usual suites + long-answer stress tests
maya: new per-layer activation histogrammer flagged concentrated tail mass in layers 21-25, mostly attention proj channels
dmitri: how many channels and how bad are we talking?
maya: about 0.4% of total channels; for those channels p99/p50 ratio > 15 and JS-divergence fp32->quant > 0.28
chris: did this correlate with specific heads?
maya: yes, tends to be head 1 and head 4 in those layers; pattern repeats across seeds and prompts
maya: observed failure mode: generation truncation + incoherent repeats for long-answer prompts under AWQ-8
chris: numbers?
maya: baseline AWQ-8 (no mitigation): throughput +24% vs fp16, long-answer ROUGE-L -5.1, perplexity +9% on long-gen set
maya: GPTQ had milder quality regression; int8-linear with per-channel clamp performed best for these prompts
dmitri: clamp how? static percentile clamp per channel?
maya: per-channel clamp to 99.2 percentile worked well; also experimented with KL-based selection to avoid clamping benign channels
alex: any perceptible runtime cost from clamping?
maya: minimal. we only store override scale/zero for ~0.4% channels; apply override during dequant path. Measured +0.5ms median latency on our 64-token batches
dmitri: what about layer-skip (keep fp16 for whole layer)?
maya: layer-skip for the worst layers (e.g., layer 23) removes regression almost entirely but throughput drops ~4.8% in microbenchmarks
chris: so tradeoff throughput vs quality. For hosted we probably prefer clamp, for Dedicated tier maybe skip
maya: proposed mitigation matrix:
- hosted (policy-hosted): per-channel clamp if JS>0.25 and p99/p50>12, clamp at 99.2 pct
- dedicated (policy-dedicated): if layer fraction of bad channels > 0.003 then keep layer fp16
- emergency (policy-fallback): fall back to FP16 output if token-level disagreement between quant and fp16 exceeds threshold
dmitri: how detect in prod cheaply?
maya: implemented lightweight profiler: sliding histogram (256-token window) per route + approx JS using 64-bin hist. Overhead ~0.6-1.0ms per request depending on batch

maya: minimal repro trace:
```
prompt: "Describe reinforcement learning with function approximation in 6 steps"
fp16: coherent ~140 tokens
awq-8: truncates ~42 tokens, repeats last sentence twice
trace: layer24.head1.channel278 p99 spike at decode step 19
```

chris: nice repro. What's the clamp config you tested?
maya: snippet we pushed in the bakeoff repo:
```
quant_mitigation_version: "v2"
per_channel_selectors:
  js_threshold: "0.25"
  p99_p50_ratio: "12.0"
clamp:
  percentile: "99.2"
layer_skip:
  check_window_tokens: "512"
  min_bad_channel_fraction: "0.003"
```

alex: add to model-onboard README please explaining why JS and p99 ratio chosen
maya: will add rationale + graphs
dmitri: rollout plan?
maya: propose canary on dedicated-gpu-2: AWQ-8 + per-channel clamp for 48h using synthetic long-gen and live traffic mirror
chris: success criteria?
maya: promote if: outlier-hit-rate < 0.05% AND long-answer ROUGE-L within -1% of fp16 AND PPL delta < +3%
dmitri: I'll add --quant-mitigation=hosted|dedicated flag to the runtime and wire in metrics: outlier-hit-rate, clamp-apply-rate, per-layer-bad-fraction
maya: ticket created ENG-ML-3497 with bakeoff table and raw traces attached; starting canary 2026-03-23 08:30 PT
qa-bot: created job ENG-ML-3497/canary-01 ETA 48h
chris: include cost delta in the ticket too
maya: AWQ-8 raw token cost -19% vs fp16; with selective layer-skip cost reduction becomes -13%
alex: minor ask: add unit tests for profiler histogram stability and a small integration test that ensures clamp doesn't change non-outlier channels
maya: on my list
dmitri: good. after canary we'll run a short experiment with hybrid: clamp + skip on worst layer to see if we can hit cost/quality sweet spot
chris: thanks team, clear mitigation path. :thumbsup:
